bayts.text: My pens have triumphed today with the two goods, if He wills Who spares me the two harms.
I have made a loan (Qurʾān 2:245) to my Lord, Allah: my being His servant and the attendant of the servant of Allah (the Prophet) in the two Abodes.
My remembrance and my gratitude (go) to Him Who has been for me, through His beloved, the Chosen One, in the two worlds.
His sufficiency — glory be to Him — (stood by me) among the enemies, and He gladdened my soul this year, on a Monday.
I have sought to thank the Withholder (Al-Qābiḍ), Who held back harm from me, and turns the two fires away from me.
I have turned my face to Him Who drove aspirations to me, He alone, and spares me the two disgraces.
I called upon Him intimately, and He answered me through him by whom I have become, for the Chosen One, like the two neighbours (Abū Bakr and ʿUmar).
O Lord, bless and grant peace in eternity, forever, to him who bestowed the two joys,
the loftiest of creatures, the best of them beyond doubt, he whose praise spares me the two evils.
My lowliness before You, through him, has become honour here: so spare me, through him, forever, the harm of the two heats.
My treasure is a Book from You, which he (the Prophet) brought us as a wise Remembrance, dispelling the two griefs.
My gain is recitation and blessing upon the Prophet, and through them You have spared me the harm of the liar.
My writings together, and the two Scribes (angels), are witnesses for me, and (likewise) the months, of this, together with the two seas.
I have held fast to the Qurʾān, a servant of the Most High (Al-ʿAlī), and He spares me the two harms through the two goods.
